name: sre

findings.message: Four new lines pipe grep's output into head -1, which exits early once it reads one line; under set -euo pipefail, grep takes SIGPIPE when call-sequence has more entries than head reads, causing the pipeline to exit non-zero inside the subshell — the assignment gets an empty string and the ordering assertions silently pass or fail on a blank.
findings.trigger: Any future test scenario that calls claim_coordinator_claim twice without resetting GHS (so POST_NOTE appears more than once in call-sequence), or a parallel test runner that appends to call-sequence concurrently.
findings.accepted_if: the four ordering-line extractions use a form that cannot receive SIGPIPE — grep directly against the file with a line-number, captured in full and trimmed in bash, or a here-string — rather than piping grep into head; and the sigpipe guard's | head scan, which now excludes -test.sh files, covers this test file or the test carries a sigpipe-ok annotation with a stated reason.

findings.message: When _ccgl_race_note_post_v returns rc 1 (POST definitively failed), and then _ccgl_remove_label also fails, the zbuild:claimed label stays on the issue; no event names the stuck label — the pipeline.claim.skipped event that the engine eventually emits says only "coordinator failed", not that the label is still there and will block the next run.
findings.trigger: A transient GitHub API outage hits both the note POST and the label-removal call in the same claim attempt; the first real API failure is expected, but the label that was successfully added moments before now has no cleanup path and no specific visibility.
findings.accepted_if: when _ccgl_remove_label fails in the backend_error cleanup paths, an event or a stderr line says the label may still be on the issue and the next run may be blocked — not only that the coordinator failed.

findings.message: The DSRACE-7 re-read of the issue after posting the holder record swallows its own failure with || true and no event or stderr line; if the re-read fails, arbitration continues with stale label state and no record of why.
findings.trigger: A momentary GitHub API error on the issue-view call that follows the note POST; the run proceeds to arbitration without any log entry that the re-read was skipped.
findings.accepted_if: a failure of _ccgl_read_labels in the DSRACE-7 re-read path produces at least a stderr line saying the re-read failed and arbitration is proceeding without fresh state.

findings.message: When the losing run's PATCH of its concurrent-claim note to "not started" fails, the failure is consumed by || true with no event or stderr line; an operator watching the issue sees the note body remain as "concurrent claim by `<holder>`" with no indication that the update was attempted and failed.
findings.trigger: A transient PATCH failure after the race is settled; the loser has already been refused, so the failure is non-blocking, but the note stays in a misleading state and nothing says why.
findings.accepted_if: a failure of _ccgl_race_note_update produces at least a stderr line naming the note id and winner so an operator can tell whether the "not started" update was lost.

reason: the sre lens found a medium or high or critical problem the change introduced
